The USPSTF recommends **biennial screening mammography** for women aged **40 to 74 years** [USPSTF, 2024]. This guidance is based on the balance of benefits and harms of screening in this population. For women aged 75 and older, the evidence is insufficient to determine the balance of benefits and harms [USPSTF, 2024]. 

This recommendation is part of the *Screening for Breast Cancer* guideline, available at [USPSTF website](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/breast-cancer-screening). 

Always consult a healthcare provider to individualize screening plans based on personal risk factors and clinical context.

results.content: The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years. Evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening in women 75 years and older.

Nitrofurantoin for 5 days or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for 3 days are first-line agents for uncomplicated cystitis in women. Fluoroquinolones are reserved for cases where first-line agents are not suitable.

Oral anticoagulation is recommended for patients with atrial fibrillation and a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 2 or more in men or 3 or more in women. Direct oral anticoagulants are preferred over warfarin in most eligible patients.

High-intensity statin therapy is recommended for patients with clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and for primary prevention in adults 40-75 years with LDL-C >=190 mg/dL or diabetes with additional risk factors.
The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years. Screening options include colonoscopy every 10 years, annual FIT testing, or stool DNA-FIT every 1-3 years.
